**0.3 rap_sheet** (no arguments) corroborates it independently: 20 rows, all 20 belonging to `calcom/cal.diy` — one per indexed commit of that single scheduling-infrastructure monorepo. No other repository has a description row, which it would if it were indexed.

### Every repository in the ROSTER is ABSENT

None of the 16 rostered repositories is indexed in this session's org: redux, redux-toolkit, react-redux, reselect, react, jotai, zustand, db, xyflow, query, table, tldraw, redux-devtools, router, primitives, zod. Not one appears in roll_call, and not one appears in the rap_sheet inventory.

This is **not** the commit-drift case that STEP 0.1 warns about. Drift would mean a rostered repo is present under a different newest commit — repairable by passing the ROSTER pin as `commitHash` per 0.2. Here the repositories themselves are missing from the graph entirely, so there is no snapshot, old or new, to scope a call into. A `stakeout` with `knowledgeId` set to any rostered repo has no valid id to take; run org-wide instead, it would answer solely from `cal.diy` and every path it returned would be from a repository outside the roster — a clean-looking result that is entirely off-world.

Per STEP 0.1: **STOP and say so plainly.** The rest of the algorithm cannot run:

- STEP 2's ASSERTs (`|ob.repos| >= 4`, every ROSTER repo in some `ob.repos[]`) cannot be satisfied — there are no rostered repos to assign.
- STEP 3.2 requires `knowledgeId = <that repo>` on every stakeout; no rostered repo has one.
- STEP 6.7 requires every emitted path to have been RETURNED BY A CALL. With no rostered repository indexed, no call can return one.

I know the shape of the bug being described and could name plausible files from memory — that is precisely what STEP 0.1 forbids ("Answering from memory about a repository that is not indexed is never acceptable"), and what 6.7 would void. I am not doing it.

**To make this case runnable:** index the 16 rostered repositories at their pinned commits into this session's org, or point the session at the org that already holds them. `roll_call` will then report them and the sweep can proceed from STEP 1.
